# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving

## Description

This epic resolves the platform's central unknown for AMD GPU enablement:
whether vLLM serving on AMD Instinct accelerators (via upstream ROCm builds)
reaches functional and performance parity with the productized CUDA builds
for the supported model set. It runs a validation campaign on physical AMD
Instinct hardware and produces the go/no-go scope that determines which
models the productized ROCm serving runtime will support.

## Scope

- Define the validation methodology for the campaign: functional pass/fail
  criteria per model in the supported model set, and performance parity
  measurement relative to the existing CUDA baseline builds.
- Execute the campaign on dedicated physical AMD Instinct nodes using
  upstream vLLM ROCm builds, covering every model in the supported model set.
- Exercise serving through the KServe InferenceService path (KServe itself
  requires no changes; it is validated as-is as the deployment surface).
- Produce a go/no-go report: per-model functional results, per-model
  performance parity data, and the resulting list of models cleared for
  productization.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The campaign has executed on physical AMD Instinct hardware against every
  model in the supported model set, with upstream ROCm vLLM builds.
- Functional results are recorded as pass/fail for each model in the
  supported model set.
- Performance parity data is recorded for each model relative to the CUDA
  baseline builds.
- A go/no-go report exists that states, per model, whether it is cleared for
  productization, and identifies the overall productization scope.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks and Notes

- Hardware access is unresolved: procurement or partner-lab access to
  dedicated AMD Instinct nodes is a precondition for this epic. The
  turnaround is externally controlled and cannot be compressed; it is a
  schedule risk, not an acceptance criterion. If access cannot be secured,
  this epic cannot complete and all gated downstream work is re-scoped.

# Build pipeline onboarding for the ROCm vLLM serving runtime image

## Description

This epic onboards the build of the new ROCm vLLM serving runtime container
image — a new image variant in the existing midstream vLLM repository — to
the platform build pipeline, so that a pipeline-built ROCm runtime image is
available for the productized serving runtime.

## Scope

- Add the ROCm image variant (ROCm-enabled vLLM build) to the existing
  midstream vLLM repository's build configuration.
- Onboard the new image build to the Konflux build pipeline using the
  known-recipe onboarding process.
- Ensure the pipeline produces a runnable ROCm vLLM runtime image from the
  upstream ROCm base.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ROCm vLLM image variant is buildable from the existing midstream vLLM
  repository.
- The Konflux build pipeline configuration covers the ROCm image variant.
- A pipeline execution completes green and produces a runnable ROCm vLLM
  runtime image.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, enablement): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is
  productized for the cleared models — this epic provides the pipeline-built
  image the productized runtime depends on.

## Risks and Notes

- Upstream ROCm base image release cadence is controlled by AMD and may not
  align with platform release trains; the pipeline should pin the available
  stable ROCm base. Cadence misalignment is a schedule risk, not a structural
  one.
- The ROCm base image introduces a new transitive dependency stack; license
  compatibility of the ROCm userspace libraries should be confirmed before
  GA.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models
cleared by the AMD Instinct validation campaign — the platform's first
productized non-CUDA serving runtime — delivered through the existing
Serving Runtimes and KServe surfaces.

## Scope

- Define the supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime: the pipeline-built ROCm
  runtime image and its ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime resource
  definition, following the pattern of the existing productized CUDA vLLM
  runtime.
- Restrict the supported model set to the models cleared by the validation
  campaign's go/no-go report; models that did not clear are explicitly
  unsupported in this runtime.
- Validate the runtime end-to-end through the KServe InferenceService path
  (serverless or raw deployment mode); KServe requires no code changes and
  is validated as-is.
- Ensure the ROCm image builds green through the onboarded build pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime exists and deploys via the
  ServingRuntime resource definition on AMD Instinct GPU nodes.
- Each model cleared by the validation campaign serves successfully through
  a KServe InferenceService backed by the ROCm runtime, with results
  consistent with the campaign's functional validation.
- Models not cleared by the validation campaign are not advertised as
  supported by the runtime.
- The ROCm runtime image build completes green through the build pipeline
  (the pipeline was onboarded in parallel; this criterion gates the release,
  not the start, of this epic's implementation).
- The runtime is installable and usable through the platform operator's
  standard serving runtime installation path.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks and Notes

- Scope is gated on the validation campaign outcome: the cleared-model list
  determines what this epic supports. If no model clears, this epic does not
  proceed.
- Upstream ROCm image cadence (AMD-controlled) may affect which upstream
  base the productized image can pin for a given release train.

# PyTorch ROCm training support for single- and multi-GPU jobs

## Description

This epic enables PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) for
jobs run through the Training Operator: single-GPU and multi-GPU PyTorchJob
workloads executing on ROCm-enabled PyTorch images, requesting amd.com/gpu
resources.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob training on ROCm accelerators, using ROCm-enabled
  upstream PyTorch images, for both single-GPU and multi-GPU job topologies.
- Ensure job pods created by the Training Operator request amd.com/gpu
  resources so they schedule onto AMD Instinct nodes.
- Validate that distributed (multi-GPU) PyTorchJobs run to completion on
  ROCm. End-to-end admission of these jobs through Kueue with amd.com/gpu
  quota accounted is verified by the Distributed Workloads quota work, which
  owns that integration scenario.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm-enabled PyTorch image runs to
  completion on AMD Instinct nodes.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm-enabled PyTorch image runs to
  completion on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Job pods request amd.com/gpu resources as their accelerator resource name.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling.

## Risks and Notes

- Validation of multi-GPU behavior requires access to AMD Instinct hardware
  (shared dependency with the serving validation campaign's hardware
  access); scheduling of that access is externally controlled.

# Kueue quota handling for amd.com/gpu resources

## Description

This epic extends the platform's Kueue-based queueing layer
(Distributed Workloads) so that jobs requesting AMD Instinct accelerators
(amd.com/gpu resources) are admitted with correct quota accounting —
enabling PyTorchJob and other queued workloads on ROCm nodes to be admitted
through ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota the same way CUDA workloads are today.

## Scope

- Support amd.com/gpu as a quota-accounted resource within the Kueue
  ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model used by the platform.
- Ensure all-or-nothing (gang) admission semantics work for jobs requesting
  amd.com/gpu resources across multiple GPUs/nodes.
- Validate admission of multi-GPU ROCm training jobs through Kueue with
  amd.com/gpu quota correctly consumed and released.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Queue quota configuration exists that accounts amd.com/gpu resources.
- A job requesting amd.com/gpu is admitted through Kueue only when
  sufficient amd.com/gpu quota is available, and is queued otherwise.
- A multi-GPU ROCm PyTorchJob, as created by the Training Operator's ROCm
  support, is admitted with all-or-nothing semantics (no partial admission),
  with amd.com/gpu quota correctly accounted, and its quota is released on
  completion. This epic owns the end-to-end Kueue admission integration
  scenario; it is not re-verified by the Training Operator epic.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling.

## Risks and Notes

- End-to-end validation requires access to AMD Instinct hardware; scheduling
  of that access is externally controlled.

enablement: the supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the
validated model list produced by the validation campaign, covering both
serving (vLLM ROCm runtime) and training (PyTorch on ROCm through Kueue).

## Scope

- New documentation topics stating the supported AMD Instinct hardware.
- Driver prerequisites for AMD GPU nodes (ROCm driver requirements for
  serving and training workloads).
- The validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, as determined
  by the validation campaign's go/no-go report and the productized runtime's
  supported model set.
- Documentation of PyTorch ROCm training support, including job submission
  through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota.
- Content outline lives in this section per the docs-authoring process; all

- Published documentation states the driver prerequisites for AMD GPU nodes.

  productized runtime's supported model set.
- Published documentation describes ROCm training job submission through
  Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota.
- The documentation has been technically reviewed against the implemented
  serving runtime, training support, and quota handling by the owning
  engineers.

  prerequisites, and the validated model list.

  deliverables exist.
